tone_statements.quote: he does not mention the floating low tone that functions as a definite marker in Maninka. … This drop in pitch is a normal phonetic manifestation of automatic downstep (Creissels 1994: 220-221). The tone remains high phonemically. … Valentine Vydrine (1999) describes it as a “descending tone, i.e. a high tone followed by a ‘floating low tone’ (the latter causes a final lowering)”. … It makes no difference whether the vowel’s tone level is high or low. … the positive phonological feature that makes a noun definite – the floating low tone – is unmarked

tone_statements.citation: Davydov, A.V. 2009. Grafika, fonetika i fonologija jazykov manden v trudax lingvisticheskoj shkoly nko [Graphics, phonetics and phonology of the Manden languages in the works of the N'ko linguistic school]. In: V.F. Vydrin (ed.), Afrikanskij sbornik - 2009. Sankt-Peterburg: MAE RAN (Kunstkamera), pp. 289-295.
tone_statements.quote: Сулейман Канте выделяет в манинка два базовых фонологических тона (kánmasere): высокий (kánmayɛlɛ) и низкий (kánmajii). Каждый из двух базовых тонов, согласно Канте, может быть падающим (kánmafanɛn или kàkɔ́dɔ) или ровным (kánnabàranɛ́n/lábaranɛn). Первое соотносится с понятием «тоновый артикль» в европейской традиции изучения языков манден. Под тоновым артиклем понимают плавающий низкий тон в постпозиции к слову. ... Для односложных слов это высокий тон и восходящий тон. У двусложников основных схем две: высокий + высокий и низкий + высокий.
tone_statements.translation: Souleymane Kanté distinguishes two basic phonological tones (kánmasere) in Maninka: high (kánmayɛlɛ) and low (kánmajii). Each of the two basic tones, according to Kanté, can be falling (kánmafanɛn or kàkɔ́dɔ) or level (kánnabàranɛ́n/lábaranɛn). The former corresponds to the notion of 'tonal article' in the European tradition of Manden studies. By tonal article is meant a floating low tone postposed to the word. ... For monosyllabic words these [standard tone schemes] are high tone and rising tone. Disyllables have two basic schemes: high + high and low + high.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 292-294 (section on tone and length notation and Kanté's tonal classes); fn. 3 p. 291 for the 'two tones, high and rising' + ideophone extra-high remark
tone_statements.summary: Two-tone system: Kanté's terms high vs low basic tones; in Davydov's (St Petersburg) terms two lexical tonemes, high and rising (LH), plus an extra-high tone only on ideophones; the 'tonal article' is a floating low tone after the noun (final-vowel lowering in isolation, lowers following words); standard schemes H / LH (monosyllables), H-H / L-H (disyllables), other words non-standard; in 'conjoi…

tone_statements.citation: Condé, Ibrahima Sory 2. 2008. Soulemana Kanté entre linguistique et grammaire: le cas de la langue littéraire utilisée dans les textes en N'ko. In: Valentin Vydrin (ed.), Mande languages and linguistics: 2nd International Conference, St. Petersburg (Russia), September 15-17, 2008. Abstracts and papers / Langues et linguistique mandé: 2e Colloque international, St. Petersbourg, 15-17 septembre 2008. Communications et résumés. St. Petersburg: Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (Kunstkamera), Russian Academy of Sciences, pp. 35-52. (Author's full text, 12 pp., posted on the conference site as files/mandelang/; volume later reprinted, ISBN 9780993996979, LoC record.)
tone_statements.quote: Kanté, très préoccupé par l’étude des tons de sa langue … il a pu noter les tons suivants à l’aide de quelques signes diacritiques : Kanmayèlè kakodo est le nom du ton haut uniforme ; Kanmayèlè labaranèn est le nom du ton haut brusque ou bref ; Kanmadjii kakodo est le nom du ton bas uniforme ; Kanmadjii labaranèn est le nom du ton bas brusque ; Kanmayèlè tèdo est le nom du ton haut neutre ; Kanmadji tèdo est le nom du ton bas neutre … il trouva douze niveaux de réalisation tonale … Il supprima quatre tons non pertinents que sont les tons neutres et il ne reste que huit tons jusqu’à nos jours.
tone_statements.translation: Kante, much concerned with the study of the tones of his language ... was able to note the following tones with a few diacritics: Kanmayele kakodo is the name of the uniform high tone; Kanmayele labaranen is the name of the abrupt or short high tone; Kanmadjii kakodo is the name of the uniform low tone; Kanmadjii labaranen is the name of the abrupt low tone; Kanmayele tedo is the name of the neutral high tone; Kanmadji tedo is the name of the neutral low tone ... he found twelve levels of tonal realization ... He removed four non-pertinent tones, namely the neutral tones, and only eight tones remain to this day.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.3 'La phonétique et la phonologie du N'ko', web p. 4; lead-in web p. 3
tone_statements.summary: Reports N'ko founder Kante's scheme secondhand: high vs low tones, each 'uniform' or 'abrupt', doubled for long vowels; 12 realizations cut to 8 written tones, length counted with tone.

tone_statements.citation: Vydrin, V.F. 2003. Tonal'nye sistemy jazykov mande: kratkij obzor [Tonal systems of the Mande languages: a short survey]. Voprosy jazykoznanija 2003(2): 95-113.
tone_statements.quote: два тональных уровня, downstep и downdrift, две тонемы, В и Н-В. Сегментной базой тонемы является слово ... Подавляющее большинство слов, вне зависимости от числа слогов, принадлежит к двум тоновым классам: высокотоновый (В, В-В...) или с восходящим тоном (Н-В, Н-Н-В, Н-В-В, и т.д.). ... Практически единственным грамматическим тоном является референтный артикль, который проявляется как плавающий низкий тон, присоединяющийся к слову (или к компактной синтагме) справа. Этот тоновый артикль отмечен в центре зоны манден (манинка, бамана, большинство идиомов дьюла)...
tone_statements.translation: [Manding, surface diversity hides a homogeneous deep structure:] two tonal levels, downstep and downdrift, two tonemes, H and L-H. The segmental base of the toneme is the word ... The overwhelming majority of words, regardless of the number of syllables, belong to two tonal classes: high-toned (H, H-H...) or rising (L-H, L-L-H, L-H-H, etc.). ... Practically the only grammatical tone is the referential article, which appears as a floating low tone attaching to the word (or compact syntagm) on the right. This tonal article is attested in the centre of the Manding zone (Maninka, Bamana, most Jula varieties)...
tone_statements.locator: p. 97, section '1. Манден' (footnote callouts 9-10 omitted in the quote)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: For Manding incl. Maninka: two tone levels with downstep/downdrift; two word-level tonemes H and LH (rising class realised L..H); domain = word or tonally compact syntagm (first member's tone spreads); toneless suffixes; floating-L referential article after the word in Maninka/Bamana/Jula; minor lexical classes (<10%, nominal); stress formation reported only for NW Manding (Kagoro, Mandinka), i.e…

tone_statements.citation: Creissels, Denis. 1987-88. Esquisse du système tonal du korokan. Mandenkan 14-15: 81-106.
tone_statements.quote: Des règles de réalisation tonale permettent de générer ces unités tonales de surface à partir de représentations sous-jacentes où figurent exclusivement deux tonèmes: haut et bas. … Le koro peut donc se décrire à partir de l'hypothèse de deux tonèmes sous-jacents, haut et bas, qui en structure se combinent pour donner des schèmes de tonalité très semblables à ceux des autres parlers manding. Dans ce qui suit, H et B représenteront en abrégé des tons affectés en structure à une syllabe, alors que h et b représenteront des tons flottants.
tone_statements.translation: Tonal realisation rules generate these surface tonal units from underlying representations that contain exclusively two tonemes: high and low. … Koro can thus be described on the hypothesis of two underlying tonemes, high and low, which combine in structure to give tonal schemes very similar to those of the other Manding varieties. In what follows, H and B abbreviate tones assigned in structure to a syllable, while h and b represent floating tones.
tone_statements.locator: p.83 (end of I. Introduction), and p.84 (II. Schèmes de tonalité sous-jacents et classes tonales)
tone_statements.summary: Koro (Manding of central Côte d'Ivoire): two underlying tones, high and low, on syllables, plus floating tones; tone spreading; downstepped high and HL contour from floating lows; nothing on stress.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: For generic 'mandingue' (a Malinké-Bambara-Dioula koine): denies lexical tone (§439); 'L'accent tonique, caractérisé en mandingue par la hauteur plus que par l'intensité, et très peu marqué en général, tombe comme en français sur la dernière syllabe du mot' (§441), placement 'soumis à une régularité absolue' (§446). sources.citation: Vydrin, Valentin & Mamadi Diané. 2014. Segmentnaja fonologija gvinejskogo maninka [Segmental phonology of Guinean Maninka]. In: A. Zheltov (ed.), Antropologija i lingvistika. Materialy peterburgskix ekspedicij v Afriku. St. Petersburg: MAE RAN, pp. 128-144. (halshs-01096618)
sources.note: Segmental phonology of standard (Maninka-Mori) Maninka; states explicitly that analysis of the tonal system is outside the article's scope, all forms given with lexical tones (fn.3: rising-tone verbs realised low in citation/pre-pausal position). No mention of stress (udarenie).

sources.citation: Vydrin, Valentin. 2014. Ton i akcent v bamana: otsutstvie korreljacii kak teoreticheskij vyzov [Tone and accent in Bamana] (talk, halshs-01076622); Vydrin, V. 2015. Nominalizacija prefiksnyx glagolov v maninka i bamana: razlichija v tonal'nom povedenii (abstract, halshs-01287438).
sources.note: Bamana 'foot stress' argued from iambic vowel reduction; remarks that in closely related Maninka 'the Bamana-type vocalic reduction is absent' (tóló, bòlón, bóló, kóló) and that Maninka's tonal system is close to Bamana's. No positive stress statement for Maninka.

sources.note: Statistical study of Maninka N'ko texts (phonemes, syllables, tone marks); 'stress' occurs only in a remark about Latin. Nothing on Maninka stress.

tone.translation: Kante, much concerned with the study of the tones of his language ... was able to note the following tones with a few diacritics: Kanmayele kakodo is the name of the uniform high tone; Kanmayele labaranen is the name of the abrupt or short high tone; Kanmadjii kakodo is the name of the uniform low tone; Kanmadjii labaranen is the name of the abrupt low tone; Kanmayele tedo is the name of the neutral high tone; Kanmadji tedo is the name of the neutral low tone ... he found twelve levels of tonal realization ... He removed four non-pertinent tones, namely the neutral tones, and only eight tones remain to this day.

tone.translation: [Manding, surface diversity hides a homogeneous deep structure:] two tonal levels, downstep and downdrift, two tonemes, H and L-H. The segmental base of the toneme is the word ... The overwhelming majority of words, regardless of the number of syllables, belong to two tonal classes: high-toned (H, H-H...) or rising (L-H, L-L-H, L-H-H, etc.). ... Practically the only grammatical tone is the referential article, which appears as a floating low tone attaching to the word (or compact syntagm) on the right. This tonal article is attested in the centre of the Manding zone (Maninka, Bamana, most Jula varieties)...
